transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-08-30 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42m
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Morales (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (Atlas Health - Head of ML), Tom Reynolds (Infra Lead), Sara Kim (Security), Eliot Gomez (Product)

Auto-generated Summary: Walkthrough focused on using Console to trace request flows, find root-cause for high latency/errors, and export request logs for audits.

00:00 Avery: ok hey everyone thanks for joining, quick intro from our side - im avery, im the AE on this account, with diego our SE, we'll do a console walkthrough today focused on tracing, error analysis and request logs for debug flows.
00:18 Priya: great thanks, main use case is clinical note summarization at scale, latency sensitive, currently on self-hosted fine-tuned model but looking to move to hosted or dedicated.
00:30 Diego: awesome, we'll jump into the console; quick note, some of the labels in the transcript might be off, fireflies sometimes garbles names.
00:45 Diego: opening the tracing view now - you can see a timeline of token generation spans per request, we group by route/model and show per-token latency heatmap.
01:10 Tom: can you show a failing request? we saw intermittent 5-7s spikes on short prompts, would like to trace root cause.
01:30 Diego: sure, filtering to last 24 hours, adding a latency > 1s filter, here's a request ID -- request_9f2c, click it to expand.
01:45 Diego: expand shows spans: request reception, routing, model inference, kv cache lookup, token emit. You can see model inference for this request is 3.9s while kv cache lookup is 10ms.
02:10 Priya: interesting, could that be cold KV cache or long compile time?
02:20 Diego: good question, sometimes compile/kernel selection can add overhead on first few calls for a model variant, but here we have repeated slow inferences across similar sequences. see the note on batch sizing - these were tiny batches so we lost batching efficiency.
02:40 Avery: remind me how batching interacts with latency SLOs?
02:45 Diego: we do continuous batching; small bursts can cause lower throughput per GPU but lower latency. for high throughput you get better tpm but higher per-request latency. you can set autoscale policy or pin dedicated capacity.
03:10 Sara: from security side we need request-level audit logs and linkage to KMS encrypted payloads. where do we get raw request logs?
03:25 Diego: request logs export is under Request Logs, you can export JSON lines containing request_id, timestamp, route, model, input hashes, and optionally full prompt/response if customer enables retention. exports can be sent to S3 or pushed to their VPC.
03:50 Priya: any redaction features? we don't want PHI to be stored by default.
04:00 Diego: yes by default hosted retention for prompt/response is 7 days unless you enable extended retention; for sensitive workloads we recommend Redwood Private or Dedicated with disabled retention, and you can use client-side KMS to encrypt payloads. We also support automatic redaction rules on the request logs - we have regex-based scrubbers.
04:35 Tom: show the error analysis pane.
04:40 Diego: error analysis groups failed requests by error code and stack traces. here's a cluster of 502s mapped to a model oom fallback, and another group of malformed JSON from a client retry loop.
05:05 Diego: clicking into the 502 cluster, you can see which instances responded and the trace shows a fallback to a smaller model variant as part of the graceful degradation policy. we surface the fallback chain and propagate the original request id.
05:30 Priya: does fallback change output semantics? we need predictable quality for clinical summaries.
05:40 Avery: great point - you can pin model versions per route; fallback is opt-in and you can configure thresholds, or disable automatic fallback for critical routes. we also have canary rollouts so you can test fallback behavior.
06:05 Eliot: can we surface prompt sets / evals when diagnosing regressions?
06:15 Diego: yes, tracing links back to the eval run if the request originated from a test harness or evaluation set, and we keep prompt-level metadata so you can replay.
06:30 Priya: show me how to run a replay.
06:35 Diego: select request, click replay - it creates a sandboxed replay that goes through the same model version and environment, and you can replay at scale with a replay job. note: replay will be charged as regular inference.
07:00 Tom: for audits, we need signed logs with KMS key rotation metadata. is that supported?
07:10 Diego: we support sending logs to your S3 with server-side encryption using your KMS, and we store rotation metadata in the audit record. for Private deployments audit logs can be shipped to your SIEM directly.
07:30 Sara: SOC2 and ISO stuff - interested in the compliance pack and SOC2 report.
07:40 Avery: I'll share our SOC2 cert and the security whitepaper after the call - also we can set up an architecture review with our security team.
07:55 Priya: back to debugging - the spike was tied to a particular GPU type?
08:05 Diego: the trace shows those slow inferences were routed to preemptible GPUs on a shared pool due to autoscaling/spot bursts; Dedicated would avoid that. you can also set routing policy to prefer on-demand capacity.
08:30 Priya: how do we test Dedicated latency? can we run a short benchmark?
08:40 Avery: yes we do benchmarking for pilot customers. we can spin up a dedicated pool for one week and run your workload set to measure p50/p95. we'll produce a benchmark report.
09:00 Diego: there was also a note about KV cache misses - look here, same prompt prefix but different tokenization variants caused cache miss. we surface tokenized prefix and can show cache hit/miss ratio.
09:30 Priya: is tokenization standardized across versions? we have custom tokenizers in our finetune.
09:40 Diego: we recommend standardizing tokenizers for caching benefits. if you have a custom tokenizer we can onboard it but it reduces cross-request cache hits unless you enable per-user cache keys.
10:00 Eliot: what about cost controls in Console?
10:05 Avery: Console has per-route cost tracking, token-level cost breakdown and can suggest quantization or smaller model variants for non-critical routes; Redwood Optimize gives quantization suggestions by workload.
10:25 Tom: can we see a live example of searching request logs for an audit?
10:30 Diego: sure - query builder supports filters by route, time, error code, and custom metadata. typing 'route:clinical-sum AND status:502' returns the relevant requests, and you can export the selected set.
11:00 Diego: small note - sometimes the transcript shows 'KV cash' or 'VPCe' instead of VPC, the auto-transcription gets weird.
11:10 Priya: (laughs) yup we've seen that from other tools too.
11:20 Diego: here's an example export schema: request_id, timestamp, user_id_hash, route, model_version, latency_ms, status_code, error_type, log_url. We can toggle full payload or hashed payload.
11:45 Priya: for pilot we need hashed user ids only, and no raw text stored.
11:50 Diego: that's straight-forward - we have a hashed-id mode and client-side encryption options.
12:05 Avery: security ask - Sara, any blockers?
12:10 Sara: need to review SOC2 docs and KMS integration details; also want to confirm RBAC for route-level access and ability to disable exports for sensitive routes.
12:25 Avery: we'll include RBAC screenshots and the export controls in the pack.
12:35 Priya: another question: how are request logs retained for Dedicated vs Hosted?
12:45 Diego: Hosted default short retention, Dedicated and Private give you options to disable retention or ship logs directly to your storage for indefinite retention per your policy.
13:00 Eliot: show an example debugging flow where a malformed json payload caused retries.
13:10 Diego: here you can see request X -> client retry loop, repeated 400s; error analysis groups them and you can link to client-side logs if they are forwarded. we also show client SDK version in metadata which helped one customer surface an old SDK bug.
13:35 Tom: can we tag routes as "no-fallback" to ensure strict model selection?
13:40 Diego: yes, route config lets you set fallback policy: allow, prefer, or disallow fallback. and you can set model pinning.
14:00 Priya: what about alerting? we want alerts on p95 > 1.2s and error rate > 0.5%.
14:10 Diego: Console has alerting rules and integrates with PagerDuty/Slack. you can create a rule on p95 latency for a particular route and severity thresholds.
14:30 Avery: quick recap: pilot with Dedicated trial, we'll run a benchmark, share pricing and SOC2/security docs, and Diego will share tracing quickstart and sample log queries.
14:55 Priya: timeline - we'd like to start pilot in the week of Sep 7, internal approvals by Sep 3.
15:10 Avery: perfect, we'll aim to deliver docs and pricing by next week.
15:25 Diego: any last questions?
15:30 Sara: nothing else, thanks for the demo.
15:35 Eliot: thanks, that was helpful.
15:40 Avery: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the pack and next steps.

End of transcript.
